Its only used when part of a question. Google "que vs qué" for more details.

That is a common misconception, even among native speakers. The diacritic in words like qué, quién, cuál, cuándo, cómo and dónde is used in both questions and exclamations, and also in sentences where they have the interrogative meaning even when the sentence itself is not a question, e.g.: Tell me what you think. --> Dime qué piensas. (or Decime qué pensás. in Argentina and other areas).

Conversely, they may appear inside a question or exclamation without the diacritic when they have the relative meaning, e.g.: How many time have I told you not to do that? --> ¿Cuántas veces te he dicho que no hagas eso? (Cuántas has a diacritic because it is functioning as an interrogative pronoun, but que does not because it is a relative pronoun)
